## Estimate an FD’s return after tax and inflation
Source: https://www.assurefintech.com/learn/savings/fd-real-return

Savings · Fixed deposits
Estimate an FD’s return after tax and inflation

Use your actual deposit terms and a clearly stated personal tax and inflation scenario—not an old bank-rate chart.

A scenario, not a bank quote

A deposit’s outcome depends on the issuer’s current rate, tenure, compounding or payout frequency, deposit amount, customer eligibility, premature-closure terms and any special conditions. Rates change, so collect them from the issuer’s official schedule for the date you plan to book. Do not use a rate in an old chart as a current offer.

For a rough comparison, estimate the effective annual return from the actual product terms. If interest is taxable for you, apply a tax assumption relevant to your circumstances and the correct assessment or tax year. Then compare the after-tax result with an inflation assumption over a matching period. State each input: the result is only as useful as those assumptions.

What the estimate leaves out

Your actual tax rate, deductions, exemptions, other income and filing position.

Deposit payout timing, reinvestment rate, tax withholding and changes in the tax rules.

Issuer-specific premature-withdrawal penalties or product conditions.

Future inflation, which is uncertain and varies across households and spending baskets.

Issuer risk and whether the deposit is eligible for DICGC protection.

TDS is not necessarily your final tax. For deposit-protection limits, aggregation and exclusions, read DICGC’s current deposit-insurance guide .

Compare deposits fairly

Compare the same tenure and payout type, and verify whether the advertised yield requires a particular customer category or amount. Consider liquidity, premature closure, maturity instructions, issuer type, deposit insurance and tax treatment—not only the highest headline rate.

Continue to our FD-offer comparison checklist or the savings hub .

Frequently asked questions
How do I estimate a fixed deposit's real return?
Start with the effective annual yield implied by the deposit's actual rate, compounding and payout terms. Apply an appropriate tax assumption to taxable interest, then compare the resulting after-tax return with an inflation assumption over the same period. The estimate is not a guaranteed future purchasing-power result.
Does TDS equal the tax I owe on FD interest?
No. Tax deducted at source is a withholding or tax-credit mechanism and is not necessarily the final tax liability. Check current tax-year rules and your own tax position.
Are bank deposits protected against loss?
Eligible deposits at an insured bank are covered subject to DICGC's limits, aggregation rules and conditions. Review the current DICGC guidance; a deposit's advertised rate does not by itself describe issuer risk or insurance coverage.

General educational information, not investment or tax advice. Rates, tax rules, deposit terms and insurance conditions can change. Verify current official terms before acting.

Separate quoted rate, credited interest and spendable interest

The stated deposit rate describes a product before your personal tax and inflation. The credited amount follows the issuer’s day-count, compounding and payout terms. Spendable interest is what remains after the applicable tax, which may differ from tax withheld by the bank. Comparing an FD with another investment requires the same after-tax basis.

For a hypothetical one-year ₹1 lakh deposit earning ₹7,000 before tax, an assumed 20% tax plus 4% cess on that tax leaves ₹5,544 interest. TDS, if deducted, is an advance credit against the final liability rather than a second permanent tax to subtract. Avoid calling the withheld percentage the investor’s true tax rate.

Use the real-return formula consistently

Real return adjusts purchasing power: (1 + nominal after-tax return) divided by (1 + inflation), minus one. With a hypothetical 5.544% after-tax return and 5% inflation, that gives approximately 0.52%, not the full 7% headline rate. Inflation and personal tax here are assumptions, not current measured values or a forecast.

For small rates, subtracting inflation gives an approximation, but use the ratio when presenting a precise example. A negative real return means reduced purchasing power under the assumptions; it does not mean the bank has deducted inflation from the account balance.

Liquidity and reinvestment change the experience

A deposit held to maturity and a deposit closed early can earn different amounts. Include the recalculated interest and any penalty when assessing an actual return. An overdraft against an FD has its own borrowing cost and does not make access to the deposit free.

When a deposit matures, the next available rate may be higher or lower. A booked fixed rate for one term does not guarantee the same income over a decade of renewals. Align maturities with planned uses and keep a separate reserve for immediate expenses.

Choose stability for the purpose it serves

A nominally stable deposit can be useful for a dated obligation even if its real return is modest. A market-linked alternative may have greater return potential but can lose value before that date. Compare risk, access and timing alongside expected return.

Review the issuer, deposit protection, ownership capacity and total balance including interest. Keep the renewal instructions and interest records accessible. A deposit should be judged against the job you need it to do rather than a promised investment ranking based on one illustrative rate.

When a low real return can still be useful

A deposit can meet an important goal even if inflation reduces purchasing power. Money for a school fee due next year has a different job from a twenty-year growth portfolio. Match maturity and access to the expense, then compare the after-tax outcome. Taking equity risk merely to beat an FD percentage can put that near-term expense at risk.

Keep three balances separate: nominal maturity value, tax still payable and purchasing power at maturity. If ₹1 lakh becomes ₹1,07,000 and the interest costs ₹2,184 tax, spendable value is ₹1,04,816. At 5% inflation, that is about ₹99,825 in today’s purchasing power. The loss is small in this one-year illustration but can compound over repeated years. It does not mean the bank failed to pay its contracted interest.

Do not double-count deposit insurance or family accounts

Several deposits in different branches of the same insured bank are aggregated in the same right and capacity. Separate account numbers or a ladder do not create a fresh ₹5 lakh limit. Joint accounts need the DICGC rules on capacity and holder order applied to the actual account arrangements. A separate banking brand also needs its legal bank identity checked.

For an amount near the insurance ceiling, accrued interest matters. If the balance starts at ₹4.9 lakh, it can grow beyond ₹5 lakh before maturity. Account for all eligible balances with that bank, including savings accounts, rather than looking only at the deposit you are about to open.

Sources for these examples and rules

DICGC: deposit insurance, aggregation and capacity

Income Tax Department: AY 2026–27 rates and deductions

Explanations revised 17 October 2026. Numerical scenarios are illustrations unless explicitly identified as issuer-published terms. Product schedules and policy documents have their own effective dates.

Convert a nominal return into purchasing power

At an illustrative 7.5% annual return and 30% tax on interest, the after-tax rate is 5.25%, ignoring cess. With assumed inflation of 5%, the exact real return is (1.0525 / 1.05) − 1 = about 0.24%, not 2.5% or 5.25%.

How to use this in your decision

Use your effective tax on the interest rather than treating TDS as the final tax. Match the return period and inflation period. An FD can still be useful for capital stability or a dated goal even when its purchasing-power gain is small.

Example assumptions: Tax and inflation are hypothetical inputs here, not current forecasts. Compounding, interest payout and tax-payment timing can change the result.

## PPF vs FD vs debt funds: compare the product, not a promised winner
Source: https://www.assurefintech.com/learn/savings/ppf-vs-fd-vs-debt-fund

SAVINGS · PRODUCT COMPARISON
PPF vs FD vs debt funds: compare the product, not a promised winner

Different liquidity, risk and tax rules mean a return table alone cannot tell you which is right for your goal.

PPF, bank fixed deposits and debt mutual funds are not interchangeable. Compare the goal, time horizon, access needs, risk tolerance, scheme conditions and tax rules that apply to you. None of the numbers in an old rate or return chart should be treated as a current quote or forecast.

Public Provident Fund (PPF)

PPF is a government small-savings scheme with a prescribed tenure and scheme-specific contribution, loan, withdrawal and extension rules. The interest rate is notified for periods and can change. Check the current notification and official scheme rules, and consider whether the long horizon and access restrictions fit your objective.

Bank fixed deposits

An FD has a stated rate and maturity or payout terms, but the offer depends on issuer, tenure, customer category and booking date. Check premature closure, payout frequency and tax treatment. Eligible bank deposits have DICGC protection only within its coverage and aggregation rules; deposits across branches of one bank are not separately insured limits. An NBFC company deposit is not DICGC-insured as a bank deposit.

Debt mutual funds

Debt funds invest in market securities; their net asset value and returns can vary with interest rates, credit quality, liquidity and expenses. They are not deposits, do not promise a fixed return and are not covered by DICGC deposit insurance. Review the scheme information document, portfolio, riskometer, expenses, exit load and applicable tax rules.

Compare these dimensions

Dimension PPF Bank FD Debt mutual fund

Return Rate notified periodically Rate fixed per deposit terms Market-linked; not guaranteed

Access Scheme-specific limits Maturity / closure terms Redemption / settlement terms

Protection / risk Government scheme rules DICGC only for eligible bank deposits, within limit Market and credit risks; no deposit insurance

Tax Check current scheme and tax rules Check current interest / withholding rules Depends on fund, dates and tax law

Use scenarios, not return promises

For a like-for-like comparison, use the same starting amount and time horizon, record each product's actual cash-flow dates and fees, and show tax separately using rules for the relevant year. For market-linked funds, test a range of outcomes rather than a single assumed rate. Keep short-term spending needs out of products whose access or value may be uncertain.

Frequently asked questions
Is PPF, an FD or a debt mutual fund safest?
They are different products with different issuers, risks, liquidity and protections. PPF is a government small-savings scheme under its rules; an eligible bank FD may have DICGC cover within applicable limits; a debt mutual fund is an investment whose value can fluctuate and is not a bank deposit. Read the relevant scheme, fund and deposit documents.
Which of the three gives the highest return?
There is no guaranteed winner across time horizons and tax situations. PPF rates are notified periodically, FD rates vary by issuer and tenure, and debt-fund returns are market-linked and not guaranteed. Compare current terms and use scenarios rather than treating a historical or assumed return as a forecast.
Can I withdraw PPF money early?
PPF has scheme-specific tenure, loan, partial-withdrawal and premature-closure rules. Check the current official scheme rules and your account's opening date before relying on access to the balance.
Are PPF, FD and debt-fund tax treatments the same?
No. Tax treatment depends on the product, investment and redemption dates, taxpayer and applicable tax year and regime. Rules can change. Verify current Income Tax Department guidance or consult a qualified tax adviser.

Related: savings guides · FD real-return guide · compare FD offers

The three products solve different timing needs

A PPF account has a long scheme-defined maturity with conditional access provisions. An FD has a selected tenure and product-specific closure conditions. A debt mutual fund holds securities whose value can move and whose redemption process follows the scheme. Treating all three as interchangeable safe savings overlooks the differences in access and risk.

Start with your goal date and whether capital may need to be withdrawn unexpectedly. Then compare the available product terms. A higher illustrative return is not useful if the money cannot be accessed when the obligation falls due.

Compare the cash-flow pattern before the yield

Periodic contributions to PPF, a single FD investment and monthly mutual-fund purchases involve different investment dates. A ten-year ending balance is not comparable unless the amount and timing invested are the same. Separate contributions from investment growth.

An FD booked at a fixed rate for one tenure does not guarantee that rate on subsequent renewals. PPF rates can change through the official notification process; do not freeze the latest rate for an entire long-term projection without labelling that assumption. A fund return is market-dependent and should not be presented as a contractual coupon.

Read the risks inside a debt fund

Debt funds can be exposed to interest-rate changes, credit events and liquidity conditions. A portfolio of government securities can still change in market value as yields move. A corporate-debt portfolio raises additional issuer-credit questions. The fund’s category, duration, holdings and Riskometer matter.

There is no DICGC insurance on mutual-fund units. Check the scheme information document, expenses, exit load and redemption timeline. A fund’s historical return during falling rates is not evidence that the next year will produce the same gain.

Compare tax and withdrawal terms separately

Product taxation can depend on the acquisition date, fund classification, tax year and investor circumstances. Verify those rules before using an old tax-efficiency chart. A contribution deduction and the tax treatment of earnings or redemption are separate questions.

Use current official PPF rules for maturity and permitted access, the bank’s FD documents for early closure, and the fund documents for redemption. A suitable combination may allocate money by goal rather than forcing every rupee into the product with the highest projected percentage.

Match liquidity and tax before projecting ten years

PPF’s annual contribution ceiling means you cannot assume a new ₹10 lakh lump sum can all enter one person’s account in one year. A ten-year horizon is also shorter than a new PPF account’s full fifteen-financial-year structure. Compare a feasible contribution schedule, not an impossible lump-sum chart.

For a debt fund, check whether section 50AA or the corresponding current provision applies to the units, their acquisition date and scheme classification. Do not carry an old indexation assumption into a new purchase. An expense ratio is already reflected in published NAV returns; subtracting it again understates those historical returns.

Match the product to the date you need the money

Suppose you need ₹3 lakh in nine months for a known expense. An investment that cannot be freely accessed by that date is not interchangeable with a nine-month deposit simply because its long-run return looks higher. A debt fund's redemption value can also fluctuate; it is not a promised bank maturity amount.

How to use this in your decision

Separate three questions: when money can be withdrawn, what can happen to principal, and how returns are taxed for your holding. Use long-horizon instruments for a long-horizon goal only after retaining accessible emergency money.

Compare the exact product and tenure

Check the issuer's official rate sheet on the day you apply. Match the tenure and deposit amount, and verify whether the quote is for a general or senior-citizen depositor, a callable or non-callable deposit, or a limited-time/special scheme. Confirm the booking date, rate lock and eligibility in the product terms.

Also compare cumulative interest with monthly, quarterly or other payout options. A payout FD and a cumulative FD do not produce the same cash-flow pattern; tax and compounding assumptions can affect a comparison.

Check liquidity and closure conditions

Read the exact premature-withdrawal rule before placing the deposit: whether early closure is permitted, the rate applied to the period actually held, any penalty or notice requirement, and whether a loan or overdraft facility is available instead. Do not assume you can withdraw at the advertised rate if plans change.

Know what DICGC insurance does—and does not—cover

DICGC's current guide states that eligible deposits are insured up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per insured bank, including principal and interest, in the same right and capacity. Deposits across branches of one bank are aggregated for this limit. Read the DICGC deposit-insurance guide for aggregation, exclusions and claim details.

Do not treat an NBFC company deposit as a bank deposit insured by DICGC. Credit ratings, guarantees and other protections are distinct from DICGC cover. Verify the legal issuer and product classification before comparing rates.

Estimate after-tax cash flow carefully

Interest taxation and tax deducted at source are governed by current rules and depend on the depositor and tax year. Withholding is not necessarily the final tax liability. Check the current Income Tax Department guidance, track interest across relevant deposits and consult a qualified tax professional if your situation is complex. Do not rely on stale thresholds or forms.

Frequently asked questions
Which bank has the best FD rate right now?
The three-bank retail snapshot checked on 17 October 2026 shows a 6.25% one-year general-public rate at SBI, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank. At three years and one day, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank list 6.50% and SBI lists 6.30%. These are selected rates for eligible deposits below ₹3 crore, not an all-market ranking.
Are small finance bank and NBFC fixed deposits insured by DICGC?
DICGC deposit insurance covers eligible deposits with insured banks, including eligible small finance bank deposits. NBFC company deposits are not bank deposits insured by DICGC. Verify the institution and product type; a credit rating is not deposit insurance.
What is the DICGC insurance limit?
DICGC states that deposits are insured up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank, including principal and interest, in the same right and capacity. Deposits held at branches of the same bank are aggregated. Check DICGC's current guide for details and exclusions.
How does premature withdrawal affect an FD?
The issuer's terms may reduce the applicable interest or apply a penalty, and some products may not allow early withdrawal. Check the exact premature-closure clause, notice requirement and payout calculation before investing.
How is FD interest taxed?
Interest is generally taxable under the applicable income-tax rules, and withholding thresholds and forms can change. Confirm the tax treatment and current TDS rules for the relevant tax year with the Income Tax Department or a qualified tax professional.

Related: savings guides · FD real-return guide · FD calculator

Compare the same maturity date and depositor category

Start with the date you need the money, then compare deposits that mature near it. A special 400-day offer and a two-year ordinary deposit solve different timing needs. Record whether the quoted rate applies to your amount, age, resident status, booking channel and callable or non-callable product. A rate available to one customer category should not be shown as the standard rate for everyone.

A cumulative deposit retains interest according to its terms; a payout deposit supplies periodic income. Match the payout frequency when comparing. An advertised annual rate is not necessarily the effective annual yield after compounding, tax and payout conventions. Use the issuer’s maturity amount for the exact product and verify whether any discounted monthly-payout method applies.

A small rate premium has a measurable rupee value

For a simple hypothetical one-year ₹5 lakh deposit, a 7% rate produces ₹35,000 interest before tax while 7.5% produces ₹37,500. The difference is ₹2,500. If the incremental interest is taxed at an assumed 30% plus 4% cess, the after-tax difference is about ₹1,720. These simple-interest assumptions are not live offers or a statement of every depositor’s tax rate.

This helps frame the decision. A higher rate may be useful, but its rupee benefit should be weighed against product access, early-closure conditions, issuer type and the effort of managing another account. Do not treat a half-point premium as a reason to disregard the nature of the deposit or its protection.

Check early closure using the period actually held

An issuer may recalculate interest using the rate applicable to the time actually completed and then apply its stated penalty. That is different from simply subtracting a penalty from the originally booked rate. Non-callable or specially restricted deposits may not provide normal voluntary early withdrawal at all.

As a hypothetical example, a two-year 7.5% booking closed after one year might use an applicable one-year rate of 6.5% less a 1 percentage-point penalty, leaving 5.5% for that illustration. The actual rate table, calculation basis and exceptions come from the issuer. Request a worked early-closure amount for the point at which you might need funds.

Leave headroom for interest in deposit-insurance planning

For eligible insured-bank deposits, the DICGC limit includes interest as well as principal and aggregates deposits in the same right and capacity at the same bank. A ₹5 lakh principal balance does not leave headroom for accruing interest under that limit. Multiple branches or multiple deposit receipts at one bank do not automatically create separate limits.

Check the legal bank name rather than relying on different account brands. A company or NBFC deposit is a different product from an insured-bank deposit; a credit rating does not make it DICGC-insured. Deposit insurance also has a claims process and is not a promise of instantaneous access to cash in every disruption. Keep emergency-access planning separate from the insurance limit.

Build a deposit ladder around actual expenses

If money is needed in stages, consider separate maturities instead of locking everything for the longest high-rate tenure. For a hypothetical ₹3 lakh goal with ₹1 lakh needed in each of three successive years, matching deposits to those dates can reduce the need to break one long deposit. The rate available when later deposits renew remains uncertain.

Track deposit number, maturity instructions, nominee, payout account and renewal setting. Auto-renewal can move money into a new term when you intended to use it. Review the bank’s rate and instructions before maturity and retain the final advice. Good administration can matter more than a small advertised premium that is lost through an avoidable early closure.

The exact annual real-return formula is (1 + after-tax nominal return) ÷ (1 + inflation) − 1. The ten-year calculation compounds that ratio. TDS is not the final tax rate: a deduction at source can be more or less than the eventual liability, and interest reporting may arise before maturity. Reinvestment assumes you can pay tax from the interest or other cash without changing the illustrated balance.

Rate changes: protect dates instead of predicting the repo cycle

A repo-rate change does not require every bank to change every FD tenure by the same amount or on the same day. A booked fixed-rate deposit and the rate available for a future renewal are different risks. If a bill is due in eighteen months, a five-year deposit with a slightly higher rate can be a poor match once early-closure rules are included.

A simple ₹6 lakh ladder might place ₹2 lakh each at one, two and three years, leaving a separate liquid reserve. As each part matures, either spend it on the planned goal or renew using then-current terms. The ladder reduces dependence on one renewal date; it does not guarantee higher returns than a single deposit. Bank-level insurance aggregation applies across those rungs.

TDS, declarations and nomination

For the AY 2026–27 rules, the specified bank-interest TDS thresholds were raised to ₹50,000 generally and ₹1 lakh for senior citizens. A TDS threshold is not an exemption from income tax. Check the form prescribed for the income period when submitting a declaration under the new Act.

Reconcile credited interest and TDS with the interest certificate and tax records. Keep the deposit advice, maturity instruction and nomination current. If a family member may need to operate the account later, understand the mandate and succession process rather than assuming a nominee becomes joint owner today.

## Senior-citizen fixed deposits: compare the terms, not just the rate
Source: https://www.assurefintech.com/learn/savings/senior-citizen-fd

SAVINGS · RETIREMENT INCOME
Senior-citizen fixed deposits: compare the terms, not just the rate

A deposit plan should balance income timing, access to cash, issuer risk, protection and tax—not maximize a headline yield in isolation.

Senior-citizen rates and eligibility differ across issuers and can change. A current official rate card and the deposit contract matter more than a rate table captured on an earlier date.

Match payout timing to expenses

Compare cumulative deposits with periodic-interest options and note the payment dates. Map known expenses and emergency cash needs before locking money away. A higher rate may not compensate for an unsuitable maturity date or a costly early-closure rule.

Check issuer and protection

Confirm whether the product is a bank deposit or a company/NBFC deposit. DICGC insurance applies only to eligible deposits at insured banks, subject to aggregation and other rules. It does not insure NBFC company deposits. Consult the DICGC guide and verify the bank's insured status.

A credit rating, issuer guarantee or promotional description is not the same thing as deposit insurance. Understand who owes the money and what protections actually apply before comparing yields.

Review closure, renewal and nomination details

Check premature withdrawal eligibility, penalties, loan-against-deposit options, auto-renewal settings, maturity instructions, nomination and joint-holder terms. Keep enough liquid funds outside deposits that cannot be accessed promptly without a cost.

Treat tax and withholding separately

Interest tax and withholding are distinct questions: TDS is not necessarily the final tax. Thresholds, forms, deductions and tax-regime treatment can change. Verify the applicable tax-year rules with the Income Tax Department or a qualified adviser; do not assume a fixed interest amount is tax-free because of age alone.

Before booking: quick checklist

Confirm current senior eligibility and rate for the chosen tenure and deposit amount.

Compare payout frequency, maturity value and premature-withdrawal terms.

Identify the legal issuer and verify whether DICGC insurance applies.

Keep near-term expenses and emergencies liquid.

Check current tax and TDS rules for the relevant tax year.

Frequently asked questions
Do all banks offer senior-citizen FD rates?
Eligibility and any additional rate vary by issuer, product, tenure and depositor. Check the current official rate card and product terms; do not assume the same premium or eligibility across institutions.
Are senior-citizen bank FDs insured?
Eligible deposits at DICGC-insured banks are covered subject to the insurance limit and aggregation rules. The cover is up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per insured bank, including principal and interest, in the same right and capacity. NBFC company deposits are not bank deposits insured by DICGC.
Does Section 80TTB mean senior citizens pay no tax on FD interest?
No blanket exemption should be assumed. Eligibility, deduction limits and regime conditions depend on the applicable tax law and tax year. Verify current Income Tax Department guidance or consult a qualified tax professional.
What should I check before booking an FD for retirement income?
Check issuer and product type, current rate, payout dates, premature-closure terms, deposit protection, tax treatment, liquidity needs and whether the maturity date fits your cash-flow plan.

Related: savings guides · compare FD offers · FD calculator

Match deposit income to the household budget

A senior-citizen rate premium can increase interest, but check eligibility, deposit type and payout frequency. Do not assume every bank or scheme offers the same additional rate. The quote may also depend on tenure, amount and whether it is a special scheme.

At a hypothetical 7.5% simple annual rate, ₹20 lakh produces ₹1.5 lakh annual interest before tax, equivalent to ₹12,500 per month on average. That average is not a guarantee of the actual monthly payout, which follows the product’s convention. Compare the credited cash with recurring expenses and keep a reserve for irregular medical or repair costs.

Cumulative and payout deposits serve different needs

A cumulative deposit builds an amount for maturity while a payout deposit helps fund current expenses. Choosing cumulative interest and then repeatedly breaking deposits for bills can defeat the purpose. Schedule maturities or payout options around actual cash needs.

Review renewal risk: a new term can have a lower rate, affecting future income. Test a budget using a lower assumed renewal rate before relying on today’s quoted amount indefinitely. Inflation can also change how far a fixed nominal payout goes.

Do not confuse withholding relief with exemption

A form requesting eligible non-deduction of tax is subject to its conditions; age alone does not establish eligibility. TDS and final tax liability are different. Check total income, the relevant year’s rules and all interest received before submitting declarations.

Use any senior-citizen interest deduction only where the applicable regime and provision allow it. Keep interest certificates, withholding records and deposit ownership details together. Do not assume a familiar historical section number applies unchanged to income under the new Act.

Check ownership, insurance and administration

Record the principal holder, joint holding, capacity, nominee and operating instructions. Deposit-insurance aggregation follows the legal bank and right and capacity, not simply the number of receipts. The limit includes accrued interest.

Review access arrangements for the person who may need to assist with banking and claims. Compare a bank FD with a senior-citizen savings scheme using the latter’s current eligibility, limits, payout and closure rules, not only a headline rate. Keep nomination and maturity instructions up to date.

What an extra half percentage point actually pays
Hypothetical ₹20 lakh; simple annual payout, constant rate, before tax. No reinvestment.
Rate Annual interest Five-year interest

6.5% ₹1,30,000 ₹6,50,000

7.0% ₹1,40,000 ₹7,00,000

Difference ₹10,000 ₹50,000

An extra 0.5 percentage point does not produce an extra ₹1.8 lakh over five years on this payout basis. Compounding produces a different difference, but it must be calculated from the stated reinvestment convention. For monthly household spending, use the actual monthly or quarterly payout quotation, not annual interest divided mechanically where the issuer discounts monthly payouts.

SCSS, deductions and a workable income reserve

Compare SCSS eligibility, maximum deposit, quarterly payout, maturity and extension terms with the selected FD. A higher quoted scheme rate is useful only if you qualify and the access conditions fit. Keep a short-notice reserve separate so a medical expense does not force premature closure of the entire income portfolio.

For AY 2026–27 under the old regime, an eligible resident senior citizen can claim up to ₹50,000 of specified deposit interest under section 80TTB, subject to its conditions. This is different from the bank’s TDS threshold. Do not claim both 80TTB and the savings-interest deduction for the same situation. Verify the corresponding provisions for the income period and include other income when checking tax and declaration eligibility.

Leave room for interest under the insurance limit

An illustrative ₹4.8 lakh one-year deposit at 7.5% grows to ₹5.16 lakh before tax under simple interest. Principal alone is below ₹5 lakh, but principal plus interest exceeds it. Other deposits at the same insured bank in the same right and capacity must also be considered.

How to use this in your decision

Make a bank-wise list of savings balances, deposits and expected accrued interest. Match payouts to recurring expenses and avoid locking the entire emergency reserve. Compare age eligibility and withdrawal rules from the actual bank offer.

## Tax-saving FD vs ELSS vs PPF: compare the trade-offs
Source: https://www.assurefintech.com/learn/savings/tax-saving-fd-vs-elss-vs-ppf

SAVINGS · TAX-RELATED PRODUCTS
Tax-saving FD vs ELSS vs PPF: compare the trade-offs

A deduction does not make two products equivalent. Compare tax eligibility, lock-in, risk and access before committing.

First confirm whether a deduction is available under the regime and tax-year rules that apply to you. Then compare the product's liquidity, risk and taxation of returns. A tax label alone is not a reason to buy an unsuitable product.

Tax-saving bank fixed deposit

A qualifying bank tax-saver FD is generally locked in for five years, and interest is generally taxable under applicable rules. Premature closure is usually restricted, subject to the scheme's terms and exceptions. Check whether the institution and product qualify, the rate and payout, the lock-in, deposit insurance and the way interest will be reported and taxed.

Equity Linked Savings Scheme (ELSS)

ELSS is an equity mutual fund and its value can fall as well as rise. Each investment generally has a three-year lock-in. Review the scheme's objective, portfolio, riskometer, costs and redemption process. Tax on redemption depends on the applicable capital-gains rules and your transaction dates; returns are not guaranteed.

Public Provident Fund (PPF)

PPF is a government small-savings scheme with a longer prescribed tenure and specific contribution, loan, withdrawal and extension rules. The notified interest rate may change over time. Check current official scheme rules and tax treatment, and make sure the tenure fits your plans for the money.

Side-by-side considerations

Feature Tax-saving FD ELSS PPF

Main risk Issuer / deposit terms Equity market risk Scheme terms and rate resets

Check the tax regime and remaining limit

Deductions under Section 80C are generally relevant to the old tax regime and are subject to a shared aggregate limit and qualifying conditions. Existing eligible payments may already use some or all of that limit. Rules may differ by tax year and instrument; verify the current Income Tax Department guidance and do not make an investment solely on an assumed tax saving.

Frequently asked questions
Do tax-saving FDs, ELSS and PPF all qualify for a tax deduction?
Eligibility depends on the instrument's statutory conditions, the taxpayer and applicable tax regime and year. Deductions under section 80C are generally associated with the old tax regime; do not assume the same deduction is available in the new regime. Confirm current law and eligibility before investing for a deduction.
Which has the shortest lock-in?
An ELSS investment generally has a three-year lock-in measured from each allotment; tax-saving bank FDs generally have a five-year lock-in; PPF has a longer scheme tenure and specific loan and withdrawal rules. Verify current product and scheme conditions before relying on access dates.
Is ELSS return guaranteed?
No. ELSS is an equity mutual fund; its value and returns can fluctuate, and capital is not guaranteed. Read the scheme information document, riskometer, portfolio and expenses, and invest only in line with your risk capacity and horizon.
Is interest from a tax-saving FD taxable?
FD interest tax and withholding are separate from any eligible deduction for the investment. Check current tax-year rules, the FD's terms and your own tax position with official guidance or a qualified tax professional.

Related: savings guides · PPF vs FD vs debt funds · tax guides

A shared deduction does not make products equivalent

Where the relevant tax period and regime permit a deduction, the benefit belongs to an eligible payment under the applicable limit. It does not guarantee the investment return. Check how much eligible deduction remains after existing contributions and payments before comparing new products.

A tax-saving bank deposit provides product-defined nominal interest, ELSS holds market-linked equity and PPF follows its government scheme. Their liquidity, risk and time horizons differ. Choose for the goal and ability to bear loss, then account for any permitted tax benefit.

Lock-in follows the actual account or purchase

A tax-saving FD normally has a five-year lock-in, while ELSS units generally have a three-year lock-in for each allotment. A monthly ELSS SIP therefore releases units on different dates rather than unlocking the entire account three years after the first contribution. Check the scheme and deposit terms for applicable conditions.

PPF maturity is based on the scheme’s financial-year rules, not three or five years from each deposit. Conditional withdrawals or premature closure do not make it an ordinary emergency account. Keep money for immediate obligations outside products whose access terms do not fit those needs.

Model the same money over the same period

Compare an identical contribution schedule. Investing ₹1.5 lakh at the start of each year and ₹12,500 monthly do not put money to work for the same length of time. Label the dates and assumed returns in any projection.

For a market-linked product, show that the projected value can differ materially and may be below contributions at a goal date. For a deposit, include the applicable tax on interest and any reinvestment after maturity. For PPF, a constant-rate projection is only an assumption if the official rate can change.

Separate entry, earnings and exit taxation

An allowed contribution deduction does not automatically make interest or sale proceeds tax-free. Each stage has its own treatment, and fund taxation can depend on the applicable rules. Use the law for the income period and actual investment rather than a blanket EEE or ETE label without conditions.

Avoid buying a long commitment only to save this year’s tax. Check fees, contribution obligations and the consequences of early exit or lapse. If existing eligible payments already fill the available cap, assess the new investment on its own merits without attributing a second deduction to it.

For an ELSS SIP, the final monthly instalment remains locked for three years from its own allotment. A three-year-old SIP does not make every unit redeemable. Select the fund for portfolio fit and risk, not an old leaderboard. Under the new regime, an investment can still serve a goal even when the old-regime 80C deduction is unavailable.

First total eligible EPF, tuition and other payments already made. A tax deduction does not make the investment free

How to use this in your decision

Choose the regime and establish eligibility before allocating money to fill a deduction limit. Then compare lock-in, contribution rules and investment risk. Do not select an equity product for money you cannot afford to see fall in value.

## Old vs new tax regime: compare using your own eligible details
Source: https://www.assurefintech.com/learn/tax/old-vs-new-regime

Tax planning · General framework
Old vs new tax regime: compare using your own eligible details

Rates, deductions, rebates and election procedures depend on the relevant tax period and taxpayer. Avoid applying a fixed deduction threshold to everyone.

Compare the tax that actually applies

Start by identifying your filing status, income sources and the year covered by your return. Income earned in periods governed by different legislation may use different names and provisions. Do not copy a slab chart or deduction limit from a different year.

Then calculate both available options using the same income details. Include salary or business income, eligible exemptions and deductions, rebates, surcharge, cess, special-rate income and any other relevant adjustments. Use the current official calculator and instructions for the relevant return. Tax software should be set to the correct assessment year or tax year.

The 2026 transition: assessment year vs tax year

For income earned from 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026, the return is for Assessment Year (AY) 2026–27 and remains governed by the Income-tax Act, 1961. Income earned from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 is Tax Year 2026–27 under the Income-tax Act, 2025. The new Act taking effect does not move FY 2025–26 income into the new tax-year system.

For Tax Year 2026–27, the new concessional regime is in section 202; deductions that are available only outside that regime use the new Act’s renumbered provisions. For example, the eligible-payment deduction formerly commonly called section 80C is under section 123 and Schedule XV, and is not available in the section 202 regime. Do not transfer an old section number or deduction assumption to a new tax year.

When using a calculator or filing portal, select the period that matches when the income was earned—not simply the calendar year in which you file. See the Income Tax Department’s official transition FAQs and its Income-tax Act, 2025 for the applicable period and exceptions.

A practical comparison checklist

Collect salary statements, interest certificates, investment and insurance records, rent and home-loan documents, and capital-gain information as applicable.

Check which claims are allowed under each regime for that exact year; do not assume that a deduction available under one is available under the other.

Confirm rebate eligibility, special-rate income treatment and any conditions for your residential or taxpayer status.

Compare final tax payable—not just slab rates or the gross value of deductions.

Review the election method and deadline, especially if you have business or professional income.

Do not change spending just for a tax deduction

A deduction reduces eligible taxable income under specified conditions; it does not make an expense free. Consider liquidity, risk, lock-in and suitability before making an investment or insurance purchase. Do not buy a product solely to reach a generic “old regime wins” threshold.

For complex income, disputed eligibility or a material difference, consult a qualified tax professional. Keep supporting documents and verify the final return before filing.

Frequently asked questions
Which tax regime is better?
There is no universal winner or deduction break-even amount. Compare your tax under the rules for the correct year, using eligible income, deductions, exemptions, rebates and special-rate income.
Which year's tax rules should I use?
Identify the year the income was earned and the corresponding return or tax year. Transitional changes mean that assessment-year and tax-year terminology may differ; use current official guidance for your situation.
Can I change regimes each year?
The available choice and timing depend on the taxpayer's income type and current law. Business or professional income can have additional election rules. Confirm eligibility and filing deadlines with the Income Tax Department or a qualified tax professional.

Try both regimes for the correct income period

Our salary tax calculator supports Tax Year 2026–27 and AY 2026–27 separately. It covers ordinary salary for resident individuals below age 60, up to ₹50 lakh, with eligible entered claims. Capital gains, employer NPS contributions and complex filing adjustments need a broader computation.

Income Tax Department: old vs new regime FAQs · Tax guides

General information, not tax or legal advice. Tax rules change and individual eligibility varies. Verify current official instructions or consult a qualified tax professional before acting.

Rebuild the comparison from taxable salary

Start with salary income for the period, not the employer’s total cost-to-company figure. CTC can include employer contributions and benefits whose treatment differs from cash salary. Reconcile the salary statement and Form 16 with the income actually included in the computation. Separate income from interest, rent, capital gains or business before using a salary-only model.

For an AY 2026–27 illustration, a resident individual below 60 with ₹15 lakh ordinary salary, no other income and only the standard deduction has ₹14.5 lakh taxable salary under the old regime and ₹14.25 lakh under the new regime. Applying the published slabs and 4% cess gives ₹2,57,400 under the old regime and ₹97,500 under the new regime. This limited example does not include surcharge, special-rate income or additional eligible claims.

Changing the old-regime assumptions changes the comparison. If the same person has an additional ₹4 lakh of genuinely eligible old-regime exemptions and deductions, old taxable income becomes ₹10.5 lakh and tax including cess becomes ₹1,32,600. If those additional eligible amounts instead total ₹6 lakh, taxable income becomes ₹8.5 lakh and tax including cess becomes ₹85,800. The examples show why neither a universal winner nor one deduction threshold works for every salary. The amounts are inputs, not a claim that every taxpayer can deduct ₹4 lakh or ₹6 lakh.

A slab, a rebate and marginal relief do different jobs

Slabs calculate tax on successive parts of taxable income. The highest applicable percentage does not apply to every rupee. A rebate then reduces eligible calculated tax under its conditions. Cess is applied to the remaining applicable tax. Keep these steps separate when checking a calculator or a worked example.

For AY 2026–27, the new-regime rebate for qualifying resident individuals can eliminate tax on ordinary total income up to ₹12 lakh. With only eligible salary and a ₹75,000 standard deduction, that corresponds to ₹12.75 lakh gross salary in this restricted illustration. It is not a general exemption for ₹12.75 lakh of any kind of income. Special-rate income and rebate eligibility require their own treatment.

Above the ₹12 lakh ordinary-income threshold, marginal relief can limit the immediate tax increase under the applicable conditions. Do not subtract the maximum rebate from every higher income or assume tax suddenly applies to gross salary at one flat rate. Use the computation for the selected period and include any special-rate income before drawing a final conclusion.

Count deductions you already qualify for before buying anything

Inventory eligible provident-fund contributions, insurance premiums, tuition payments, rent-related exemption, loan-interest claims and other applicable amounts. Check the relevant limits and conditions separately. A total payment to a product is not necessarily the allowed deduction, and the same payment cannot be counted twice.

For example, if a combined deduction limit is already filled by existing eligible payments, buying another product will not increase the deduction under that limit. Keep additional personal NPS contribution and employer NPS contribution separate: they have different provisions and conditions. The site’s salary calculator does not model every employer contribution or complex return adjustment.

A tax saving is also not the entire invested amount. An illustrative ₹1 lakh deduction at a 30% marginal rate with 4% cess saves ₹31,200 if the full deduction actually reduces income taxed at that rate and no other interaction changes the result. The remaining money is still committed to the expense or investment. Evaluate lock-in, liquidity and risk before chasing a deduction.

Payroll selection and return filing are separate steps

Tell payroll which regime and documented claims should be used for withholding, then review the eventual return using the applicable election rules. Tax deducted from salary is a credit against final tax, not proof that the selected computation is correct. A refund or additional payment can arise when other income or final eligible claims differ from payroll estimates.

Taxpayers with business or professional income can face different election procedures and restrictions from salary-only taxpayers. Do not copy advice about changing regimes annually without identifying the income type. Check the relevant form, deadline and year before making the election.

The 2026 legal transition makes the period especially important. Income for FY 2025–26 still belongs to AY 2026–27 under the 1961 Act; income from April 2026 uses the new tax-year terminology and renumbered provisions. The figures above are explicitly AY 2026–27 examples. The current-period selector in the calculator should be used for a different period rather than silently reusing old section references.

Review the final comparison before filing

Use the same complete income base for both available options. Reconcile interest certificates, capital-gain records, withholding and eligible exemptions. Check age and residential status where they affect the calculation. A salary example for someone below 60 cannot be transferred unchanged to a pensioner whose old-regime basic threshold differs.

Keep a short worksheet recording gross income, each allowed adjustment, taxable income, slab tax, rebate or relief, surcharge where applicable and cess. Compare the final liability and retain the supporting evidence. This makes a difference between payroll and the return explainable instead of treating the lower number as automatically correct.

A retired taxpayer: pension and interest are not one salary input

Consider an AY 2026–27 resident aged 65 with ₹12 lakh ordinary employment pension and ₹2 lakh eligible bank-deposit interest. Assume old-regime eligible 80C payments ₹1.5 lakh, eligible 80TTB deduction ₹50,000, no other income or claims and no surcharge. Old taxable income is ₹11.5 lakh after the ₹50,000 pension standard deduction and stated claims. Using the senior-citizen old slabs gives ₹1,61,200 including cess. This example distinguishes ordinary employment pension from family pension, which has a different deduction rule. It also keeps interest separate from salary. It is not an output of the site’s under-60 salary model. A real retired household should reconcile each pension/interest certificate and age/residential-status condition before using the figures.

Surcharge, employer benefits and the filing choice

Above ₹50 lakh, surcharge and its separate marginal-relief rules enter the comparison. AY 2026–27 ordinary-income surcharge rates begin at 10%, then 15% and 25%; the old regime can reach 37% above ₹5 crore, while the new regime maximum is 25%. Certain income types have specific caps. Our calculator stops at ₹50 lakh instead of pretending that a salary-only result includes these effects.

Ask payroll to distinguish basic salary, allowances, reimbursements and eligible employer pension contributions. A genuine eligible employer contribution is different from your personal NPS contribution, and an expense reimbursement requires its own conditions. A change in CTC labels does not automatically create an exemption. Compare the employer cost, take-home cash and restrictions, not just the tax percentage.

The employer’s TDS selection and the regime used in the return are separate steps. Business or professional income can trigger different option forms, deadlines and limits on switching back. Keep the filed option acknowledgement and use the form for the applicable year. A salaried example should not be applied to a freelancer without checking those rules.

## Tax-saving investments: verify the deduction before investing
Source: https://www.assurefintech.com/learn/tax/80c-beyond-the-obvious

Tax planning · Deductions
Tax-saving investments: verify the deduction before investing

An investment’s tax treatment depends on the applicable tax year, regime and eligibility—not only its product label.

First identify the law and regime

For income earned from 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026, a return filed for AY 2026–27 remains under the Income-tax Act, 1961; the deduction is still commonly called section 80C. For income earned from 1 April 2026 onward, the Income-tax Act, 2025 uses Tax Year 2026–27 and reorganizes the corresponding eligible-payment deduction under section 123 and Schedule XV. In that new Act, section 123 is not available if you choose the default concessional regime under section 202. Use the correct official calculator and the rules for the exact period.

Worked example: the combined limit is not per product

For an individual eligible to use the old regime for AY 2026–27, suppose the year’s eligible EPF contribution is ₹70,000, qualifying life-insurance premium is ₹35,000, and qualifying tuition fees are ₹55,000. The total is ₹1,60,000, but the combined section 80C/80CCC/80CCD(1) limit is ₹1,50,000. The excess ₹10,000 does not create another deduction under this combined limit.

That is a limit illustration, not a conclusion that every payment qualifies. Check who paid, who is covered, policy or investment conditions, payment timing and the regime. For Tax Year 2026–27, the corresponding section 123/Schedule XV deduction also has a ₹1,50,000 cap, but is unavailable in the section 202 new regime.

Separate tax treatment from product suitability

Tax-saving products can differ substantially in risk, liquidity, lock-in, fees and returns. A market-linked fund is not equivalent to a deposit or a government-backed scheme. Compare each product’s official documents and consider your investment goal and ability to bear losses. A deduction, if available, does not guarantee that an investment is appropriate or profitable.

NPS, provident-fund contributions, insurance premiums, tuition-related payments and other eligible items may have different conditions. Do not double-count amounts or treat an employer contribution the same as your own payment. If unsure, ask a tax professional before making an irreversible investment or filing a claim.

Frequently asked questions
Does every taxpayer get a deduction for 80C investments?
No. Eligibility depends on the applicable law, tax regime, taxpayer and nature of the payment or investment. Check current official guidance and your specific return instructions.
Is NPS always an extra deduction?
NPS tax treatment depends on the contribution type, taxpayer, employer arrangement, applicable regime and year. Check the current rules; do not assume that every contribution qualifies for an additional deduction.
Should I invest in ELSS only for tax savings?
No. ELSS is a market-linked mutual fund and can lose value. Assess its risk, investment horizon, lock-in, costs and suitability, along with whether a deduction is actually available to you.

Income Tax Department: AY 2026–27 deductions and regime rules · section 123 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 · official section 123 and new-regime FAQ · Tax guides

General educational information, not tax, investment or legal advice. Verify current rules and eligibility with official sources or a qualified adviser.

Start with payments already made during the year

For a period and regime where the deduction is available, list eligible employee provident-fund contributions, qualifying life-insurance premium, tuition fees, housing-loan principal and other eligible payments already made. Each has conditions. Do not assume every insurance premium, education bill or property payment qualifies simply because it resembles a category in a tax-saving advertisement.

Create a ledger with payer, beneficiary, date, amount, applicable provision and supporting receipt. Reconcile the employee contribution separately from an employer contribution. The combined limit is applied after eligibility checks; it is not a separate allowance for each product.

Understand the saving before filling the remaining limit

If ₹1.2 lakh of eligible payments already fills a hypothetical ₹1.5 lakh combined limit, only ₹30,000 remains under that limit. A further ₹70,000 investment does not produce a ₹70,000 deduction there. An unused limit is an option to evaluate, not an obligation to buy a product.

The value of a deduction depends on the tax computation. It reduces eligible taxable income rather than refunding the investment. A taxpayer with no tax remaining after an applicable rebate may receive no additional immediate saving from another deduction. Compare the final liability before committing cash.

Match the product to the goal and lock-in

A deposit, provident-fund account, equity-linked fund and insurance contract have different risks, access rules and purposes. A tax-saving label does not turn market returns into a guarantee or make a long-duration insurance commitment equivalent to a short savings account.

Set aside emergency and near-term spending money before selecting a locked product. Compare ongoing charges, surrender or premature-closure rules, investment risk and the amount needed in later years. A hurried March purchase can create a multi-year obligation for a one-year deduction.

Keep separate provisions separate

An additional contribution deduction or a health-insurance deduction does not automatically enlarge the combined savings-payment cap. Read the relevant provision, qualifying person and limits. Personal NPS and employer NPS require different treatment, and one contribution should not appear under two deductions.

For income from April 2026, use the corresponding provisions of the 2025 Act, including section 123 and Schedule XV where applicable, rather than transferring the old section label without checking the regime. Retain the payment certificates and the calculation used in the final return.

Check existing payments before opening a new product

If employee EPF already uses ₹90,000 and eligible tuition uses ₹60,000, the ₹1.5 lakh combined ceiling is filled. Another ₹50,000 investment may fit your financial plan, but it does not create another ₹50,000 deduction inside that filled limit. A ₹1.5 lakh deduction saves ₹46,800 only where the whole amount reduces income otherwise taxed at 30% plus 4% cess, without other interactions.

NPS and liquidity are separate decisions

The additional personal NPS deduction under section 80CCD(1B) can be up to ₹50,000 where eligible under the old regime. Do not claim the same contribution twice under two sections. Employer NPS under section 80CCD(2) follows separate salary-linked rules and can be relevant to the new regime; it is not a second label for your personal investment.

Choose an instrument after matching the goal and liquidity needs. A tax-saving FD, PPF and ELSS do not become equivalent because a deduction appears under the same ceiling. Locking an emergency reserve in a product you cannot redeem can cost more than the tax saved. Use the corresponding provisions and section numbers for Tax Year 2026–27 rather than copying an old return’s section numbers.

Find the unused limit before buying something

For a hypothetical taxpayer eligible for Section 80C, suppose employee PF contributions are ₹90,000 and qualifying life-insurance premiums ₹30,000. These already total ₹1.2 lakh. Under the ₹1.5 lakh limit for AY 2026–27, only ₹30,000 remains; a further ₹1 lakh purchase does not create a further ₹1 lakh deduction.

How to use this in your decision

Reconcile contributions and eligible payments already made during the year. Confirm the regime and eligibility first. A product's maturity, risk and insurance suitability still matter; avoid unnecessary purchases just because a sales illustration assumes a full deduction.

## HRA exemption: calculation, eligibility and records
Source: https://www.assurefintech.com/learn/tax/hra-calculation

Tax planning · Salary and rent
HRA exemption: calculation, eligibility and records

Use the applicable tax-year instructions and your payroll details; a calculator cannot establish eligibility by itself.

General calculation structure

For an eligible salaried taxpayer, the HRA exemption is generally the lowest of: (1) HRA received from the employer; (2) rent paid less 10% of the relevant salary; and (3) the prescribed 40% or 50% salary limit, depending on the applicable city classification. The salary definition and exact conditions are set by the tax rules; check the current instructions before using the formula.

Worked example for AY 2026–27

Assume a salaried employee in Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata or Chennai has, for each of 12 months, basic salary plus eligible DA of ₹60,000, HRA of ₹30,000, and actually paid rent of ₹35,000. Under the stated assumptions:

HRA received: ₹30,000 × 12 = ₹3,60,000.

Rent minus 10% of salary: (₹35,000 − ₹6,000) × 12 = ₹3,48,000.

50% of salary: ₹60,000 × 50% × 12 = ₹3,60,000.

The lowest amount is ₹3,48,000, so that is the illustrative exemption; ₹12,000 of the ₹3,60,000 HRA remains taxable. This example assumes rent and salary were unchanged for all 12 months and uses AY 2026–27 rules. It is not a TY 2026–27 calculation under the Income-tax Act, 2025.

Eligibility and documents

Confirm HRA was received as part of eligible salary and that the chosen tax regime permits the claim.

Use rent actually paid for the relevant period; do not claim a notional amount.

Retain rent receipts or other evidence, rental agreement if applicable, salary statements, and payment records.

Provide any landlord or payment details required by the employer or return forms.

Check current rules if renting from a relative; the arrangement must be genuine and properly documented.

Frequently asked questions
Can I claim HRA under the new tax regime?
The availability of HRA exemption depends on the applicable regime and tax-year rules. The Income Tax Department's current guidance for the return period says HRA exemption is available under the old regime and not the new regime; check the current rules for the year you are filing.
How is HRA exemption generally calculated?
For eligible salaried taxpayers, the exemption is generally based on the least of actual HRA received, rent paid less 10% of the relevant salary, and the prescribed 40% or 50% salary limit depending on the applicable city classification. Verify the exact salary definition and rules for your year.
What records should I keep for an HRA claim?
Keep salary records, rent receipts or other proof of rent, landlord details and any required payment evidence or declarations. Documentation requirements can depend on the amount and the return rules for the year.

Income Tax Department: salaried taxpayer guidance for AY 2026–27 · official transition guidance for Tax Year 2026–27 · compare tax regimes

General educational information, not tax or legal advice. Verify the correct tax year, eligibility and documentation requirements before filing.

Use the salary definition and the relevant period

For the AY 2026–27 old-regime calculation, the relevant salary definition is not total CTC. Basic salary, qualifying dearness allowance and turnover-based commission have the specified treatment. Match the salary, HRA received, rent paid and location for the period being calculated. A change in employer, salary, rent or city can require separate period calculations.

The exemption is the least of actual HRA received, rent paid minus 10% of relevant salary, and 50% of relevant salary for the specified metro cities or 40% elsewhere, subject to eligibility. The specified cities are Mumbai, Kolkata, Delhi and Chennai; everyday use of the word “metro” does not automatically place another city in that tax category. These are AY 2026–27 rules, not an assumption about every regime or period.

Work through one example instead of deducting the whole rent

Assume an eligible old-regime AY 2026–27 case with ₹6 lakh relevant annual salary, ₹2.4 lakh HRA received and ₹2.16 lakh actual rent paid for the same period outside the specified metros. The three amounts are ₹2.4 lakh, ₹1.56 lakh and ₹2.4 lakh. The least is ₹1.56 lakh. The remaining ₹84,000 of received HRA is not exempt under that calculation.

This example assumes the stated amounts meet all eligibility conditions. If rent changes halfway through the year, do not substitute a full year of the later rent. Calculate the appropriate periods and keep payment evidence. A negative rent-minus-salary component does not create a negative exemption.

Documentation should support a genuine rental arrangement

Keep the agreement, receipts or payment trail, landlord details and the evidence requested by payroll and the applicable filing rules. Payments to a related person need the same underlying reality of tenancy and payment; a receipt alone does not turn living rent-free into an eligible rental expense.

Payroll may request documents and apply withholding based on submitted claims. The return still needs a correct claim for the actual period and regime. Reconcile the salary certificate and reported exemption rather than assuming every amount payroll accepted is automatically final.

Home ownership and HRA require separate eligibility checks

Owning a property does not by itself answer whether rent paid elsewhere qualifies for HRA exemption. Nor does receiving HRA establish eligibility for a home-loan-interest deduction. Residence, property use, payments and the applicable provisions must be considered separately.

If you do not receive HRA, do not use the HRA formula as a substitute for any other rent-related deduction. That other provision has its own conditions and filing requirements. For the new regime or the new Act’s tax year, confirm which exemption is available before carrying this old-regime example into a calculation.

Mumbai, Delhi and Bengaluru: one salary, different rent
FY 2025–26 / AY 2026–27 old regime. Assume ₹6 lakh annual qualifying salary and ₹3 lakh HRA received. HRA salary is not automatically gross CTC.
Residence Annual rent Rent less 10% of salary City ceiling Exempt HRA

Mumbai ₹3,60,000 ₹3,00,000 ₹3,00,000 (50%) ₹3,00,000

Delhi ₹2,40,000 ₹1,80,000 ₹3,00,000 (50%) ₹1,80,000

Bengaluru ₹3,60,000 ₹3,00,000 ₹2,40,000 (40%) ₹2,40,000

The exemption is the lowest of actual HRA, rent minus 10% of qualifying salary, and the applicable 50% or 40% ceiling. Bengaluru is not one of the four cities eligible for the 50% ceiling under this rule; the four are Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata and Chennai. If rent or employment changes during the year, split the calculation into the relevant periods.

Tax saved is not the HRA exemption itself. A ₹1.8 lakh exemption reduces taxable income; the tax reduction depends on your slabs, rebate position and other facts. Do not multiply the exemption by 30% if the deduction crosses more than one band or changes rebate eligibility.

Rent paid to parents and a home loan in another place

A genuine rental arrangement with a parent requires an actual tenancy, rent payments and consistent records. The parent needs to account for rental income under the applicable rules. A fabricated receipt without rent paid is not a tax strategy. Keep the agreement, receipts and bank trail, and supply landlord details required by payroll or the return.

Owning a property does not by itself settle an HRA claim. Where you actually live, why you rent, the ownership and use of the other property, and the home-loan deduction conditions all matter. Work out HRA and property-income treatment separately; claiming both needs facts that support both. Do not claim HRA for living in your own house.

Do the calculation period by period

For an illustrative non-metro month, assume ₹60,000 qualifying basic salary, ₹30,000 HRA and ₹25,000 rent. The three amounts are actual HRA ₹30,000, rent less 10% of salary ₹19,000, and 40% of salary ₹24,000. The lowest is ₹19,000, making ₹11,000 of that month's HRA taxable if the exemption is otherwise available.

How to use this in your decision

Recalculate when salary, HRA, rent or location changes rather than multiplying one favourable month by twelve. Keep the tenancy and payment evidence. Verify what counts as salary for this exemption and whether your chosen regime allows it.

## Credit-card rewards and tax: check how the benefit arose
Source: https://www.assurefintech.com/learn/tax/tax-on-credit-card-rewards

Tax planning · Card rewards
Credit-card rewards and tax: check how the benefit arose

There is no safe universal answer for every kind of points, cashback, promotion or business-card benefit.

First identify the type of benefit

Rewards earned as part of a personal purchase, cash or points awarded for a promotion, referral benefits, and rewards attached to business expenditure raise different factual questions. The issuer’s label is useful evidence but does not, by itself, decide the tax treatment.

Start with the card and promotion terms, statement, redemption record and any tax certificate or withholding information. Record whether the spending was personal, reimbursed, or incurred for an employer or business, and who was entitled to use the resulting benefit.

Examples: what to document before deciding

Points earned on personal shopping: save the statement and redemption record, and note whether the reward reduced the purchase cost or was awarded separately.

A promotional prize or referral reward: retain the offer rules and any communication or tax certificate from the payer; check the tax year and applicable reporting or withholding rules.

Rewards generated by business or employer spending: keep the expense and reimbursement records and check who owns the benefit under the employer’s policy. Do not treat it as personal income or a tax-free discount without establishing the facts.

These are record-keeping examples, not tax classifications. Similar-looking rewards can have different facts and treatment.

Questions to resolve for your situation

Was the benefit a reduction in the price of something you bought, a separate prize or payment, or compensation for a referral or activity?

Was it earned through personal spending or business/employer spending?

Was tax withheld, and is there a certificate or information in your tax records?

Which tax year and reporting rules apply, and does the benefit need to be reported under your circumstances?

Where the amount is material, the treatment is unclear, or a business/employer is involved, ask a qualified tax professional. Do not rely on a general article or social-media interpretation as a filing position.

Frequently asked questions
Are personal credit-card reward points always tax-free?
Do not assume that every reward or redemption has the same tax treatment. The facts—including whether the benefit is a purchase-linked discount, prize, referral benefit, employer-provided perk or business-related reward—may matter. Check current official guidance or obtain individual tax advice.
Are prizes from a card promotion treated like ordinary reward points?
A prize or promotional win may be treated differently from a benefit linked to ordinary purchases. Review the promotion terms and current tax and withholding rules, and retain any tax certificate or communication from the payer.
What if I use a company card for business spending?
Follow the employer's expense and rewards policy. Ownership and personal use of benefits earned from business spending can raise employment and tax questions; ask your employer and a qualified tax professional rather than assuming the points are personal or tax-free.

For reporting or withholding questions, start with the Income Tax Department’s current guidance for the relevant tax year . Keep the underlying statement and offer terms alongside your return records. · Tax guides

Reviewed September 28, 2026. This guide explains which facts and records to check; it does not classify every reward or determine an individual filing position.

Identify what the benefit actually represents

A reduction in the purchase price, cashback associated with a purchase, a reward point, a contest prize and a referral payment do not necessarily have the same factual character. Record why the benefit was received, who paid it and whether it relates to a personal purchase or a business activity. The app’s label alone does not settle tax treatment.

Keep the purchase invoice and benefit record together. A cash reward visible in an account is different from an unredeemed point balance with restrictions. Do not announce that every reward is tax-free or that every point must be treated as cash income at an assumed conversion rate.

Business spending needs consistent accounts

Where a purchase is recorded as a business expense, examine how a linked discount or cashback is treated in the books and the relevant tax rules. An invoice recorded at full cost and a later related benefit should be reconciled, rather than ignored because it arrived through a credit-card programme.

Separate personal and business transactions, retain statements and document who owns the reward under employer or company policy. Rewards earned on reimbursed expenses may also raise accounting or policy questions beyond the individual cardholder’s preferences. Seek a qualified review for material amounts.

Referral and promotional payments deserve separate attention

A benefit for introducing a customer or performing a promotional activity is a different event from a price reduction on goods you bought. Record any campaign terms, payment certificate and withholding information. An issuer describing the payment as a reward does not eliminate the need to identify its nature.

Similarly, a competition prize or business-linked incentive should not be folded into a blanket statement about ordinary retail cashback. Match the facts to the applicable tax period and provision. A threshold from an unrelated gift rule is not proof that all benefits below it can be ignored.

Use records to resolve uncertainty

Create a ledger for significant benefits showing the associated transaction, nominal amount, redemption, date and intended accounting treatment. Reconcile it to statements and any tax information made available by the payer. Avoid counting a hypothetical catalogue valuation as money received.

If the treatment is material or unclear, take the actual terms and records to a tax professional. A useful question specifies the activity, payer, personal or business context and whether the benefit was cash or restricted redemption. That produces a more meaningful answer than asking whether credit-card rewards in general are taxable.

Keep purchase rebates, business adjustments and prizes separate

A rebate attached to your own personal purchase, a business incentive, an account-opening award and a contest prize are different facts. A single blanket statement that all rewards are taxable—or that every reward is tax-free—loses those distinctions. Retain the offer, purchase invoice, statement credit and redemption record so the nature of the receipt can be established.

For business books, identify whether a credit relates to a specific recorded purchase and how the expense, inventory or asset was recorded. Do not record the full expense and then silently omit the linked credit. Income-tax treatment, GST input tax credit and accounting presentation are separate questions; a reward arriving on a personal card does not by itself answer any of them.

An overseas hotel redemption is not automatically rupee cash income equal to the hotel’s highest retail price. Keep the points spent, co-payment, actual benefit and programme terms. Where classification is material or unclear, give those records to the person preparing the return. A card statement alone does not establish a statutory exemption.

Income Tax Department: AY 2026–27 rates and deductions

Explanations revised 17 October 2026. Numerical scenarios are illustrations unless explicitly identified as issuer-published terms. Product schedules and policy documents have their own effective dates.

Classify the transaction before assigning tax treatment

A household purchase of ₹10,000 followed by a ₹500 statement credit leaves a net purchase cost of ₹9,500. A business recording that purchase as an expense must avoid retaining the full ₹10,000 deduction while silently ignoring the linked credit. That accounting question differs from the taxation of a standalone promotional prize.

How to use this in your decision

Keep a record of the purchase, reward type, statement credit and whether the purchase was personal or business. Do not extrapolate one treatment to referral incentives, prizes, miles or transferred rewards. A meaningful business amount warrants review of the underlying documents.

Example assumptions: An accounting illustration, not a blanket legal conclusion that every reward is taxable or tax-free.
